stories.title: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars
stories.summary: A new study tracking 13 astronauts suggests that the human heart may be surprisingly well equipped for a journey to Mars, especially with regular exercise during spaceflight.

stories.title: Just 4 minutes a day can dramatically improve strength after 65
stories.summary: A new Penn State study suggests that just four minutes of daily strength training can significantly improve mobility and physical function in older adults.

stories.title: Scientists find 10 different diets linked to slower aging
stories.summary: A study by DZNE finds that healthy eating is associated with slower biological aging—and that there is more than one way to eat healthily.

stories.title: Inside Health
stories.summary: Experts warn poor at-home injecting techniques and new drugs mean new health risks.

stories.title: Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why statins, the widely prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs that help prevent heart attacks and strokes, can sometimes cause muscle pain, weakness, and even severe muscle damage.

stories.title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable
stories.summary: The aging brain may be undergoing a remarkable transformation rather than simply losing its abilities, shifting its focus from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture.

stories.title: Scientists find a way to fight Alzheimer’s brain damage without removing toxic tau
stories.summary: Scientists have found a promising way to protect the brain from Alzheimer’s-related damage by blocking immune cells that contribute to the destruction of neurons.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between vitamin C and cancer survival
stories.summary: A surprising clinical trial suggests that taking vitamin C daily could improve survival in people with precancerous blood disorders and early-stage blood cancers.

stories.title: Why some people escape Alzheimer’s despite carrying a high-risk gene
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered why some people with a high genetic risk of Alzheimer’s remain mentally sharp into their 80s, uncovering a rare mutation that protects the brain from harmful protein buildup.

stories.title: Just 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer's, scientists find
stories.summary: Walking just 3,000 steps a day could help slow Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, according to new research. Scientists discovered that physical activity was linked to less buildup of harmful tau proteins and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, even in people already showing early…

stories.title: Scientists win 2026 Nobel Prize for controlling brain cells with light
stories.summary: A discovery in tiny algae led to a Nobel Prize-winning breakthrough that allows scientists to switch brain cells on and off using light. The revolutionary technique has already helped researchers activate memories and is opening new possibilities for restoring vision and treating brain disorders.

stories.title: "Mind-blowing" Alzheimer’s breakthrough: Two hours of sleep restored without clearing brain plaques
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected culprit behind sleep loss in Alzheimer’s disease: overactive immune cells in the brain. By temporarily removing these cells, researchers restored more than two hours of sleep per day in mice, revealing a promising new target for treatment.

stories.title: Is it true that … you need to take 10,000 steps a day to be healthy?
stories.summary: The fitness benchmark has surprisingly unscientific origins – yet it does contain more than a kernel of truth The idea that we need to walk 10,000 steps a day originated not in medical research but in a 1960s marketing campaign for a pedometer, says Jack McNamara, senior lecturer in clinical…

stories.title: Modern neuroscience is rediscovering a surprising idea freud had 130 years ago
stories.summary: Researchers have identified striking parallels between Sigmund Freud’s century-old theories and modern neuroscience, suggesting that the brain’s constant predictions shape how we experience reality.

stories.title: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt
stories.summary: Eating too much salt may do more than raise blood pressure. It could also harm memory and social behavior. In a new study, Japanese researchers discovered that a soy-derived compound called LPC70 helped protect mice from several damaging effects of a high-salt diet.

stories.title: Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood
stories.summary: Eating blueberries every day could have surprising effects on mood, according to a small study that found greater reductions in depressive symptoms among older adults who consumed the fruit for three months.

stories.title: Scientists uncover 3 key brain pathways linked to lasting depression relief
stories.summary: Researchers have uncovered three brain pathways linked to lasting improvements in people receiving deep brain stimulation for severe, treatment-resistant depression.

stories.title: Scientists find a youth protein that helps aging brain cells act young again
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that a protein linked to youth helps protect the brain’s immune cells from age-related decline.

stories.title: New drug reverses severe fatty liver disease by repairing the gut
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that a potential new drug can reverse severe fatty liver disease in animal models by restoring gut health and blocking harmful substances from reaching the liver.

stories.title: Brain cells meant to protect us may be fueling cognitive decline
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising cause of age-related cognitive decline involving brain cells previously thought to be entirely beneficial.

stories.title: Scientists discover how deep sleep builds muscle, burns fat, and boosts the brain
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising two-way relationship between sleep and growth hormone, revealing how the brain carefully balances physical recovery with wakefulness.

stories.title: Yale scientists discover how stress changes the brain to make memories stronger
stories.summary: Yale scientists have uncovered how the stress hormone cortisol helps the brain turn emotional experiences into stronger, longer-lasting memories.

stories.title: Scientists discover how exercise reverses muscle aging
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological mechanism that helps explain how exercise can reverse some of the damage caused by muscle aging. The key is a gene called DEAF1, which becomes overactive with age and interferes with the muscles’ ability to clear damaged proteins and repair themselves.

stories.title: Mysterious brain activity under anesthesia challenges what we know about consciousness
stories.summary: Even under general anesthesia, the human brain can analyze language, recognize different types of words, and predict what comes next in a story, according to a surprising discovery by Baylor researchers.

stories.title: Rare study reveals a striking divide inside an Alzheimer’s patient’s brain
stories.summary: A rare examination of an Alzheimer’s patient’s brain revealed that regions cleared of amyloid plaques had remarkably little of the harmful tau buildup associated with memory loss, while neighboring areas showed extensive damage.

stories.title: Menopause is a biological transition that’s become a lucrative consumer business
stories.summary: While menopause media coverage helps to bust taboos, it also fosters a lucrative, social media and business-driven market that takes advantage of woman’s need for support.

stories.title: Strokes have nearly doubled among younger adults, and scientists aren't sure why
stories.summary: Strokes are becoming alarmingly common among younger adults, with rates nearly doubling among people ages 20 to 54 over nearly three decades.

stories.title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to rare risk of sudden vision loss
stories.summary: Popular diabetes and weight loss drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy have been linked to a slightly increased risk of a rare condition that can cause sudden, potentially permanent vision loss.

stories.title: A 47-year study reveals the age when your body starts losing strength
stories.summary: A 47-year study has uncovered a surprising turning point in physical aging: fitness and strength begin declining around age 35, even among people who exercise regularly.

stories.title: Cancer is rising in younger adults, and scientists can't fully explain why
stories.summary: A major study found that several cancers are rising faster among younger adults in England, even as smoking, diet, and other established risk factors have generally improved.

stories.title: Decade-long gym steroids study shows just what happens to men's hearts
stories.summary: One of the first long-term studies that followed weight-training middle-aged men for nearly a decade has found that consistent use of anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) leads to the thickening of the heart’s left ventricular wall, which increasingly reduces the organ's ability to function.

stories.title: Scientists reveal why some workout recovery tricks can backfire
stories.summary: Ice baths, massages, compression garments, and recovery supplements promise faster muscle recovery, but research suggests their benefits are often overstated, and some techniques may even undermine long-term gains.

stories.title: Scientists may have overlooked a hidden Alzheimer's culprit for decades
stories.summary: For decades, scientists have focused on amyloid beta as a major culprit behind Alzheimer’s disease, spending billions of dollars developing treatments that have often delivered disappointing results.

stories.title: Scientists discover how harmful “zombie cells” hide from the immune system
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a protein that may help harmful aging cells hide from the immune system, allowing them to accumulate and fuel age-related health problems.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising paradox in how our cells age
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that the body's cellular recycling system behaves very differently during aging than previously believed, with higher activity sometimes linked to worse physical health.

stories.title: The secret to handling stress better may start at breakfast
stories.summary: Your daily routine could have a bigger impact on your ability to handle stress than you realize. A Binghamton University study of approximately 400 college students found that eating breakfast regularly, exercising, sleeping well, and taking fish oil were associated with greater psychological…

stories.title: Scientists uncover a hidden map of the brain with 539 distinct regions
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden layer of organization in the brain by creating the first detailed 3D map of its lipids, the fatty molecules essential for brain structure and communication.

stories.title: After 30 years, scientists finally have a drug for a deadly brain disease
stories.summary: The FDA has approved the first drug that directly targets Alexander disease, a devastating neurological disorder affecting fewer than one in a million people.

stories.title: Scientists find a hidden problem with endless smartphone scrolling
stories.summary: Excessive smartphone use may be taking a hidden toll on the brain and body, with heavy scrolling linked to poorer memory, reduced attention, disrupted sleep, and potential balance problems.

stories.title: Scarred blood vessels may be one clue to APOE4’s Alzheimer’s risk
stories.summary: Scientists know APOE4 raises Alzheimer’s risk. A surprising change in blood vessel cells may help explain how.

stories.title: Popular weight loss drugs linked to a surprising fingernail problem
stories.summary: Popular GLP-1 weight loss drugs, such as Ozempic and Wegovy, have been linked to unexpectedly high rates of nail detachment, hair loss, and scalp inflammation, with some problems occurring several times more frequently among users.

stories.title: Scientists find hidden driver of aging and a simple amino acid that fights memory loss in mice
stories.summary: Scientists discovered that declining levels of a protein called Menin may help drive aging, and restoring it in older mice reversed several age-related changes in just 30 days.

stories.title: Just 10 minutes of daily exercise could unlock deeper sleep
stories.summary: Getting better sleep might be as simple as moving a little more every day. Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin found that people who exercised more frequently experienced more deep, restorative sleep, which is essential for brain recovery, memory, and emotional well-being.

stories.title: The hidden math of Alzheimer's could point to new treatments
stories.summary: Mathematics may hold unexpected clues to understanding Alzheimer’s disease. Scientists have developed a model showing how common metals like copper and zinc may influence the buildup of proteins associated with the disease, while also exploring possible ways to stop the process.

stories.title: Eating olive oil before carbs has a surprising effect on blood sugar
stories.summary: A simple change in the order you eat your food could help prevent blood sugar spikes. Scientists discovered that giving mice olive oil before carbohydrates slowed digestion and activated a surprising combination of hormones and nerve signals that helped regulate blood sugar, even in mice with type…

stories.title: A surprisingly simple way to relieve knee arthritis pain without pills or surgery
stories.summary: A surprisingly simple change in how you walk could help relieve knee arthritis pain and even slow joint damage. In a year-long clinical trial, researchers found that adjusting the angle of a person's foot while walking reduced osteoarthritis pain by an amount comparable to medication, without…

stories.title: Scientists discover 5 hidden brain patterns behind depression
stories.summary: Depression may not be one biological condition, but several distinct patterns of brain activity hiding under the same diagnosis.

stories.title: Only one workout helped older adults lose fat and keep muscle
stories.summary: A six-month study suggests that high-intensity interval training (HIIT) may offer older adults a powerful advantage: losing body fat while keeping their muscle.

stories.title: Nearly 30,000 people tested quit-smoking methods. One stood out
stories.summary: Nicotine e-cigarettes appear to help more smokers quit than patches, gum, and several other common approaches, according to a major review of 80 clinical trials.

stories.title: Scientists tested 5 natural compounds on cancer cells. One stood out
stories.summary: Five natural compounds, including curcumin and berberine, were tested for their effects on cancer cells and healthy muscle cells. All disrupted cancer cell energy production and pushed many of the cells into a non-dividing state, with curcumin producing the strongest overall effect.

stories.title: FDA-approved epilepsy drug may help reverse osteoarthritis damage
stories.summary: Researchers at Yale have identified a promising new approach to osteoarthritis that could do more than simply ease pain. The epilepsy drug lacosamide appears to block a protein involved in both pain signaling and cartilage destruction, helping damaged joints shift back toward repair in preclinical…

stories.title: An experimental drug kills fat cells, rather than shrinking them
stories.summary: Participants in two small trials lost dangerous fat around their internal organs. This fat is linked to health issues like diabetes and heart problems.

stories.title: Just 7 days of strength training started shrinking fat cells in mice
stories.summary: Just seven strength-training sessions helped obese mice shrink visceral fat cells and reactivate molecular pathways involved in burning stored fat, despite no change in overall body weight.

stories.title: Scientists warn a popular vitamin D supplement may have a hidden downside
stories.summary: Not all vitamin D supplements are created equal, and new research suggests that one popular form may have an unexpected downside.

stories.title: Gene therapy and special goggles give some blind people limited sight
stories.summary: Optogenetics, recognized by the 2026 medicine Nobel, makes cells respond to light, including eye cells that normally relay signals to the brain.

stories.title: Drug target could block brain inflammation linked to Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s
stories.summary: Blocking a receptor called P2X7 significantly reduced inflammation in human brain tissue, revealing a potential new treatment strategy for neurological and psychiatric disorders.

stories.title: Goodbye joint replacements? Stanford scientists found a way to regrow cartilage and stop arthritis
stories.summary: Scientists have found a surprising way to regrow damaged knee cartilage by blocking a protein that becomes more abundant with age.

stories.title: Scientists say this simple habit could strengthen your marriage
stories.summary: Couples who exercise together report better communication, healthier conflict resolution, and lower marital stress than those who work out alone. Even something as simple as taking a walk together may create valuable opportunities to talk, listen, and feel more connected.

stories.title: A few drops of this Japanese tree oil may help you sleep more soundly
stories.summary: In a small study, sleeping near the scent of Hinoki root essential oil was linked to fewer nighttime awakenings, better morning alertness, and brain-wave changes associated with smoother sleep onset.

stories.title: Vagus Nerve Stimulation Could Help New Skills Stick
stories.summary: Stimulating the vagus nerve after practice helped mice develop stronger long-term motor learning, revealing a potentially important window when the brain is still locking in a new skill.

stories.title: Your gut bacteria may reveal how fast your brain is aging
stories.summary: A UCLA study links faster brain aging to specific gut bacteria and chemical byproducts, with older-looking brains also associated with poorer memory, focus, and mood.

stories.title: This common vitamin could help fight one of the deadliest brain cancers
stories.summary: High-dose vitamin B3 is showing intriguing early promise as an addition to standard glioblastoma treatment, with 82% of patients in a small trial remaining progression-free after six months.

stories.title: Vitamin D drug may help crack pancreatic cancer’s protective shield
stories.summary: A vitamin D analog may help break down pancreatic cancer’s protective defenses, potentially making tumors more vulnerable to chemotherapy and immune attack. A small clinical trial found encouraging responses, especially in patients whose tumors had high levels of the vitamin D receptor.

stories.title: Diet drinks work as well as water for weight loss, major trial finds
stories.summary: A two-year randomized clinical trial involving 493 adults with overweight or obesity found that diet soft drinks were essentially as effective as water for long-term weight loss and weight maintenance.

stories.title: Leucine does more than build muscle. It powers up your cells
stories.summary: The essential amino acid leucine can boost cellular energy production by protecting key proteins on mitochondria from being destroyed. The discovery reveals a new connection between nutrition and metabolism that could eventually lead to new approaches for metabolic disorders and cancer.

stories.title: Your gut may be making a molecule that raises Alzheimer’s risk
stories.summary: Scientists have linked a gut bacterial compound called ImP to greater Alzheimer’s risk, harmful brain protein buildup, and faster cognitive decline. The finding raises the possibility that reducing ImP in the blood could one day help slow or prevent dementia.

stories.title: Vitamin C linked to fewer deaths in blood disorder trial
stories.summary: Vitamin C may do more than support the immune system. In a phase 2 trial of people with precancerous or low risk blood cancers, daily vitamin C did not slow abnormal cell growth, but it was linked to favorable changes in inflammation and fewer serious complications.

stories.title: Cancer stem cells have an “energy addiction” scientists may be able to exploit
stories.summary: High-risk MDS stem cells appear to have an unexpected “energy addiction,” relying far more heavily than healthy blood-forming cells on a molecule called NAD. Disrupting this energy pathway selectively weakened the cancer-driving cells, revealing a potential new target for treatment.

stories.title: This diet may slow brain aging by 2.5 years
stories.summary: People who followed the MIND diet more closely showed slower brain shrinkage and less grey matter loss over time, with the strongest differences equivalent to about 2.5 years of delayed brain aging.

stories.title: Could quitting ultra-processed food boost your mental health?
stories.summary: People with depression who dramatically cut ultra-processed foods experienced notable improvements in their symptoms in a small preliminary study. Researchers suspect healthier eating may benefit the brain partly by reducing gut damage and chronic inflammation.

stories.title: Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may have a reversible weakness
stories.summary: The Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may actively damage brain blood vessels and sabotage the cellular systems that remove harmful proteins.

stories.title: Creatine may help build muscle even without exercise, researchers find
stories.summary: Creatine helped middle-aged adults gain muscle and strength even without a structured workout program in a new 12-week study. When combined with exercise and a calorie-reduced diet, it produced even greater strength gains while helping participants add lean tissue and lose fat.

stories.title: Brain scans reveal which disorders are linked to faster brain aging
stories.summary: A massive MRI study found that Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment, psychiatric disorders, and addiction are associated with distinct patterns of accelerated brain aging.

stories.title: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
stories.summary: A new study suggests coffee may influence mood and brain function by changing the activity of microbes in the gut. Both caffeinated and decaf coffee were linked to lower stress, depression, and impulsivity, while also producing measurable changes in gut bacteria and metabolites.

stories.title: 160-million-year-old proteins show surprising power against superbugs
stories.summary: Scientists resurrected antimicrobial peptides from mammals that lived millions of years ago and found that some were more potent against drug-resistant bacteria than modern human versions.

stories.title: Resetting the body clock could help the brain recover after stroke
stories.summary: Strengthening the body’s natural daily rhythms helped mice recover after stroke by improving the brain’s waste-clearing system and reducing lingering inflammation.

stories.title: Scientists found a surprising driver of Alzheimer’s outside the brain
stories.summary: Scientists found that immune cells contributing to Alzheimer’s-related brain damage may be activated in lymph nodes outside the brain before traveling into the nervous system.

stories.title: Glucosamine, a popular joint supplement, linked to faster Alzheimer’s progression
stories.summary: A large health-record analysis found that glucosamine use was associated with a 25% higher likelihood of mild cognitive impairment progressing to dementia.

stories.title: Why rheumatoid arthritis pain may persist even when inflammation is under control
stories.summary: Pain and fatigue in rheumatoid arthritis can persist even after inflammation improves, with depression, poor sleep, obesity, smoking, and chronic pain potentially helping sustain symptoms.

stories.title: ‘It’s problematic’: concern as weight-loss jab maker sponsors Vogue World event
stories.summary: Critics say partnership between Mounjaro maker Eli Lilly and fashion giant suggests thinness is an aspiration The fifth iteration of Vogue World , overseen by Anna Wintour, took place in Milan on Tuesday night.

stories.title: Scientists say house cats could help unlock better cancer treatments for humans
stories.summary: Scientists have mapped the genetics of cat cancer on an unprecedented scale and found surprising similarities with tumors in humans. The findings could help bring precision cancer treatments to cats while also revealing new clues about how human cancers develop and respond to drugs.

stories.title: REM sleep paradox: Dreaming may drain the brain’s energy even as fuel supply rises
stories.summary: Scientists discovered a surprising energy paradox in the brain during REM sleep, the stage most closely associated with dreaming. Blood supply to the brain begins increasing even before REM starts, but neurons’ immediately available energy, measured as ATP, then drops.

stories.title: Scientists gave worms magnetic bacteria. They lived 43% longer
stories.summary: A magnet-producing bacterium extended the average lifespan of C. elegans worms by more than 43% while helping protect their neurological and intestinal health.

stories.title: Aging muscles may be losing strength for a reason scientists missed
stories.summary: A newly identified breakdown in communication between nerves and muscles could help explain why people lose strength as they age. Researchers were able to improve muscle strength in an animal model by targeting a key protein, raising hopes that some age-related weakness could eventually be treated.

stories.title: Breakthrough drug reverses skin aging and dramatically speeds healing
stories.summary: A topical drug that removes aging, damaged cells helped older mice heal skin wounds significantly faster. The treatment appeared to reactivate repair pathways involved in inflammation, collagen production, and new blood vessel growth.

stories.title: This new drug could break cancer’s resistance to treatment
stories.summary: A new experimental drug called CS18 may help break through cancer drug resistance by disabling several of the defenses tumors use to survive treatment. It strengthened existing therapies, restored drug sensitivity in resistant lung cancer cells, and slowed tumor growth in animal models.

stories.title: Coffee doesn’t have to keep you awake to disrupt your sleep
stories.summary: Caffeine may make sleep less restorative even when you fall asleep normally and stay in bed for eight hours, with EEG recordings revealing fewer of the slow brain waves associated with deep sleep.

stories.title: Brain scans reveal a possible cause of long COVID fatigue and brain fog
stories.summary: Researchers have found evidence that long COVID may damage dopamine releasing neurons in the brain, potentially explaining persistent fatigue, low motivation, slowed movement, and memory difficulties. The discovery could lead to new treatments that target the brain's dopamine system.

stories.title: Stem cells reverse stroke damage and restore movement in mice
stories.summary: Stem cell transplants helped regenerate stroke-damaged brain tissue in mice, producing new neurons and restoring lost motor function.

stories.title: Scientists create a needle-thin brain implant that can do three jobs at once
stories.summary: A new needle-thin brain implant can record neural activity, deliver drugs, and stimulate multiple brain regions using a single flexible fiber.

stories.title: Chronic stress may be quietly reshaping your heart
stories.summary: Chronic inflammation tied to stress, lifestyle, mental health, and socioeconomic conditions may silently change the heart for years before any symptoms appear.

stories.title: Stanford scientists discover the human brain may actually be two separate organs
stories.summary: Scientists have found that the human brain develops from two distinct cellular systems, suggesting that evolution fused together two ancient nervous systems with very different jobs.

stories.title: A new start after 60: I’m 92 and cycling is my life – despite the crash that left me unconscious
stories.summary: Arthur Plummer got a bike when he retired at 65 and joined a cycling club as one of its youngest members. Now he is its oldest but still racking up 5,000km every year When Arthur Plummer retired at 65, he bought a secondhand bicycle.

stories.title: Millions take calcium and vitamin D for bone health. A major review finds little benefit
stories.summary: A sweeping review of more than 153,000 adults found that calcium and vitamin D supplements, alone or together, do little to prevent fractures or falls in most older people.

stories.title: These blood thinners may have an unexpected benefit for Alzheimer’s patients
stories.summary: Newer blood thinners may do more than prevent strokes in people with Alzheimer’s disease and atrial fibrillation. Researchers found that patients taking NOACs experienced a slower decline in cognitive function than those using warfarin or no blood thinners.

stories.title: Scientists restore a brain protein and reverse signs of aging in mice
stories.summary: Scientists found that declining levels of the brain protein Menin may help drive aging, with lower levels in mice linked to inflammation, cognitive decline, weaker bones, and thinner skin.

stories.title: This popular fermented food may help flush nanoplastics from the body
stories.summary: A kimchi-derived bacterium can bind to nanoplastics under gut-like conditions and may help carry them out of the body. In mice, the probiotic more than doubled the amount of nanoplastics detected in feces, pointing to a surprising potential use for microbes from fermented foods.

stories.title: New mesothelioma drug turns cancer’s own defenses against it
stories.summary: Scientists are testing a counterintuitive way to fight mesothelioma, an aggressive asbestos-linked cancer with few effective treatments. A new experimental mesothelioma drug kills cancer cells by disabling PRX3, an antioxidant defense that tumors use to survive intense oxidative stress.

stories.title: Scientists find an immune “false alarm” that may drive rapid aging
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that some severe genetic disorders linked to rapid aging may be driven not just by damaged DNA, but by the body’s overreaction to that damage.

stories.title: Scientists find the whole grain “sweet spot” for better heart health
stories.summary: Eating four to six servings of whole grains a day may deliver meaningful benefits for heart health, according to a large review of 87 clinical trials. Researchers found improvements in body weight, waist size, blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar, triglycerides, and some markers of inflammation.

stories.title: Ultra-processed foods linked to hidden muscle fat that may threaten your knees
stories.summary: Eating more ultra-processed foods was linked to greater fat buildup inside thigh muscles, according to MRI scans of 615 adults at risk for knee osteoarthritis. Surprisingly, the association remained even after researchers accounted for calorie intake, physical activity, and other factors.

stories.title: Scientists reversed biological age in older adults in just 4 weeks
stories.summary: Older adults who changed the balance of fat, carbohydrates, and animal protein in their diets showed signs of reduced biological age after just four weeks. The strongest result appeared in participants eating an omnivorous, lower-fat, higher-carbohydrate diet.

stories.title: Smelling chocolate helped men complete more reps without feeling more tired
stories.summary: Simply smelling chocolate helped men complete more leg extension repetitions without making the workout feel harder, with dark chocolate producing the strongest effect. The researchers think familiar food aromas may influence appetite and motivation by making the brain anticipate eating.

stories.title: Scientists discover a major brain shift between ages 50 and 75
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered sweeping changes in how the human brain controls and organizes its genome beginning in midlife, offering new clues to why aging sharply increases the risk of Alzheimer’s and other neurodegenerative diseases.

stories.title: Nearly 10,000 patients reveal what works best for knee arthritis pain relief
stories.summary: A major analysis of 139 clinical trials involving nearly 10,000 people suggests that some of the simplest treatments may work best for knee osteoarthritis.

stories.title: Cancer is rising in younger adults. Faster biological aging may help explain why
stories.summary: Cancer rates are rising in adults under 55, and new research suggests accelerated biological aging may be one piece of the puzzle.

stories.title: Hidden brain wiring may help keep the mind sharp as gray matter shrinks
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that the brain’s short-range wiring may help protect cognition even as gray matter shrinks with age. Healthier connections just beneath the brain’s surface were linked to better language skills and appeared to weaken the impact of gray matter loss.

stories.title: Scientists find a hidden cause of high blood pressure that routine tests can miss
stories.summary: A wearable device has revealed nighttime hormone surges that may expose a frequently missed cause of high blood pressure. The discovery could help explain why primary aldosteronism often escapes standard blood tests and point toward a more accurate way to diagnose it.

stories.title: Scientists discover strange link between low vitamin D and pain
stories.summary: Low vitamin D levels may make recovery from breast cancer surgery more painful, according to a study of 184 women undergoing mastectomy.

stories.title: Scientists find a new layer of Alzheimer’s hidden in the genome
stories.summary: Scientists found that the 3D organization of DNA is disrupted in several types of brain cells affected by Alzheimer’s disease, altering how important genes are switched on and off.

stories.title: AI uncovers hidden Ozempic side effects across 400,000 Reddit posts
stories.summary: AI analysis of 400,000 Reddit posts found that users of drugs such as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound reported unexpected symptoms including menstrual changes, chills, hot flashes, and fatigue.

stories.title: Scientists find Ozempic may slow aging itself
stories.summary: Semaglutide helped older healthy mice live longer while improving memory, muscle function, blood sugar control, and several biological signs of aging.

stories.title: The secret to longer life may be hidden in bat DNA
stories.summary: Long-lived bats appear to combine powerful immune defenses with unusual strategies for eliminating damaged cells, potentially helping them avoid cancer and disease for decades. Researchers hope these genetic tricks could eventually reveal new ways to protect human health during aging.

stories.title: Scientists find signs of extreme aging and youth in the same 117-year-old
stories.summary: A remarkably detailed study of Maria Branyas, who lived past 117, reveals that extreme longevity may involve both intense aging and powerful biological protection at the same time.

stories.title: Scientists discover the human heart can regrow muscle after a heart attack
stories.summary: Researchers have shown for the first time that human heart muscle cells can regrow after a heart attack. The finding overturns the idea that damaged areas of the heart are completely incapable of regeneration.

stories.title: DNA treatment cuts bad cholesterol by nearly 50% without statins
stories.summary: Researchers have designed a new DNA-based treatment that targets PCSK9, a protein closely tied to high LDL cholesterol and atherosclerosis.

stories.title: Scientists find a bone-building switch that could fight osteoporosis
stories.summary: An experimental compound called AP503 significantly strengthened bones in mice by activating GPR133, a receptor that boosts bone formation while slowing bone loss.

stories.title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to nearly 40% fewer asthma attacks
stories.summary: Semaglutide, the drug found in Ozempic and Wegovy, was linked to nearly 40% fewer asthma attacks in a large real-world study. It was also associated with about 20% fewer COPD flare-ups.

stories.title: Ozempic and Wegovy may have an unexpected mental health benefit
stories.summary: Semaglutide, the drug behind Ozempic and Wegovy, may have benefits that extend well beyond weight loss and diabetes. In a large Swedish study of nearly 15,000 people with bipolar disorder, its use was linked to a 21% lower risk of psychiatric hospitalization.

stories.title: Early statin use linked to 15% lower dementia risk
stories.summary: Starting statins soon after a type 2 diabetes diagnosis may do more than protect the heart. In a nationwide Danish study of more than 132,000 people, those who began statin treatment within a year of diagnosis had a 15% lower relative risk of developing dementia over 10 years compared with those…

stories.title: Popular brain supplement linked to shorter lifespan in men
stories.summary: A large study involving more than 270,000 people has linked higher blood levels of the amino acid tyrosine to a shorter lifespan in men.

stories.title: This lifestyle program improved cognition 55% more than basic health advice
stories.summary: Older adults at risk of dementia improved their memory and thinking after following lifestyle programs combining exercise, healthy eating, cognitive training, and social engagement.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden problem with this popular sugar substitute
stories.summary: Sorbitol, a sugar alcohol commonly used in sugar-free candy, gum, and other low-calorie foods, may not be as harmless as it seems. Researchers at Washington University in St.

stories.title: Stanford scientists discover a seafood that can reverse signs of aging
stories.summary: A substance found in edible sea squirts appeared to reverse several signs of aging in older mice. Plasmalogen supplements improved memory and learning, strengthened connections between brain cells, reduced inflammation, and even helped the mice grow thicker, darker hair.

stories.title: Scientists reveal the hidden instructions that build the human brain
stories.summary: UCLA researchers have discovered two powerful influences that help guide how the human brain forms before birth. Radial glia, stem cells responsible for producing much of the cerebral cortex, change their behavior depending on how they process glucose and on physical contact with signals arriving…

stories.title: New injectable treatment helps the brain rebuild after stroke
stories.summary: Duke researchers developed an injectable scaffold that helped stroke-damaged brains grow new blood vessels, support nerve regrowth, and recover movement in mice.

stories.title: One immune switch may help drive aging across the body
stories.summary: Aging may be partly fueled by immune cells losing their ability to clear away damaged, inflammation-promoting cells. Blocking a single receptor restored that cleanup process in mice, reducing inflammation and helping their organs, muscles, and memory remain remarkably youthful.

stories.title: Anti-aging benefits of exercise achieved with mini-muscle implants
stories.summary: Frequent resistance training and cardiovascular workouts are critical for maintaining our mental and physical health as we age.

stories.title: “Broken heart syndrome” can look just like a heart attack. This test can tell them apart
stories.summary: “Broken heart syndrome” can mimic a heart attack so closely that patients often need invasive testing to tell the difference. Researchers have now developed the BioTAK score, which combines biological sex with blood biomarkers to identify the condition before cardiac catheterization.

stories.title: Money problems may age your brain faster
stories.summary: Persistent financial hardship in early and middle adulthood was linked to poorer thinking skills by the 50s and more signs of brain aging later in life. Researchers say years of chronic stress and financial worry may gradually take a toll on the brain.

stories.title: Alzheimer’s may leave a mark on the brain long before plaques appear
stories.summary: Brain changes associated with Alzheimer’s may begin at least seven years before amyloid plaques become detectable with current PET scans. Researchers uncovered the signal by tracking healthy older adults with repeated brain imaging over nearly 20 years.

stories.title: Too much coffee may weaken bones, study finds
stories.summary: Following nearly 10,000 older women for 10 years, researchers found that tea drinking was associated with slightly higher hip bone density. Moderate coffee consumption did not appear harmful, but drinking more than five cups a day was linked to lower bone density.

stories.title: Your neighborhood in your 20s may shape your heart decades later
stories.summary: Where you live in early adulthood may quietly shape your heart health for decades. Researchers found that adverse neighborhood conditions were linked to a higher risk of coronary artery calcification in midlife, an early warning sign of cardiovascular disease.

stories.title: Obesity leaves a lasting memory in immune cells
stories.summary: Obesity appears to leave a molecular imprint on key immune cells that may persist for 5 to 10 years after weight loss. This long-lasting “obesity memory” could help explain why some obesity-related health risks remain elevated even after body weight returns to normal.

stories.title: Reaching 90 without dementia doesn’t mean you’re in the clear
stories.summary: A study of people over 90 found that dementia risk remains strongly shaped by sex, race and genetics, with women and black participants facing notably higher risks.

stories.title: High blood sugar may help cancer cells hide from the immune system
stories.summary: Researchers discovered a possible way cancer cells hide from the immune system: they build a thick, sugar-rich coating around themselves. High blood sugar can strengthen this protective shield under conditions that resemble the environment inside tumors, with the protein HSF1 playing a key role.

stories.title: Scientists challenge a 70-year-old “lizard brain” myth
stories.summary: A long-standing picture of brain evolution as newer, rational layers stacked on top of an ancient “lizard brain” may be deeply misleading.

stories.title: Common supplements rival antibiotics for severe gum disease
stories.summary: Omega-3 and low-dose aspirin matched the effectiveness of antibiotics in a year-long study of patients with severe gum disease, with both approaches helping about 58% reach the treatment goal.

stories.title: Researchers unveil sustainable spirulina solution to vitamin B12 deficiency
stories.summary: Researchers have produced a form of Spirulina containing biologically active vitamin B12 at levels comparable to beef. By carefully controlling the light used to grow the algae, they overcame a major problem with conventional Spirulina, which mainly contains a form of B12 the human body cannot use.

stories.title: Keto diet cut liver fat by 67% in a clinical trial
stories.summary: A ketogenic diet outperformed Mediterranean and low-fat diets in several measures of metabolic health during a clinical trial involving people with obesity, prediabetes, and fatty liver disease.

stories.title: Dogs may hold surprising clues to human longevity
stories.summary: Dogs and humans may have more in common when it comes to aging than scientists realized. Researchers with the Dog Aging Project found that patterns of small molecules in dogs’ blood were linked to longer or shorter lifespans in remarkably similar ways to those seen in people.

stories.title: Long-term melatonin use linked to 90% higher heart failure risk
stories.summary: People with chronic insomnia who used melatonin long term had a roughly 90% higher risk of developing heart failure over five years, according to a large preliminary study.

stories.title: Your sleep may be hiding an early clue to Alzheimer’s
stories.summary: Frequent micro-awakenings during sleep were linked to higher genetic risk for Alzheimer’s in healthy middle-aged adults who had no symptoms. The discovery raises the possibility that subtle changes during sleep could offer an early warning signal years before memory problems appear.

stories.title: Experimental eye drops help blind mice see again
stories.summary: Scientists have created light-activated drugs that helped blind mice perceive light again and restored visually guided behavior without gene therapy, implants, or specialized lighting.

stories.title: Longevity is yours to control, as this obscure city of 'super-agers' shows
stories.summary: Clusters of towns and cities around the world have become curious case studies for scientists looking into just how residents there appear to defy natural aging, living healthier for much longer than anywhere else on the planet. Now, another "longevity hotspot" is in the spotlight.

stories.title: Scientists may have found a shortcut to calorie restriction’s anti-aging benefits
stories.summary: Moderate calorie restriction lowered an immune protein called C3 that appears to help drive chronic inflammation as the body ages.

stories.title: Childhood trauma may leave a lasting “scar” inside brain cells
stories.summary: Early-life stress may physically alter how DNA is packaged in the brain, leaving stress-related genes primed to activate more easily years later. In mice, researchers were able to block this effect, preventing the heightened anxiety and stress sensitivity that otherwise appeared in adulthood.

stories.title: Your genes may decide whether a low-carb diet sends cholesterol soaring
stories.summary: A low-carb diet may raise LDL cholesterol much more sharply in people who are genetically predisposed to high cholesterol, particularly when they consume lots of saturated fat. The findings could help explain why people following seemingly similar diets can have dramatically different results.

stories.title: Depression may shut down the brain’s ability to make new neurons
stories.summary: A major study found that adults with depression show disrupted production of new neurons in the hippocampus, potentially weakening the brain’s ability to separate new experiences from painful memories.

stories.title: Too much or too little sleep may make your body age faster
stories.summary: Both too little and too much sleep may be linked to faster aging throughout the body. Researchers analyzing 23 biological aging clocks found the lowest aging levels among people sleeping about 6.4 to 7.8 hours per day.

stories.title: Broccoli for women, beans for men? Study reveals sex split over healthy diets
stories.summary: A new study has found that eating more legumes was associated with better cardiometabolic health in young men, while cruciferous vegetables such as broccoli and cauliflower were the prime choice of vegetable for young women.

stories.title: A major Alzheimer’s risk gene may shrink brain cells years before symptoms
stories.summary: Researchers have uncovered a possible reason why the Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 can disrupt the brain long before memory problems begin. In mice, APOE4 increased a protein called Nell2, shrinking neurons and making memory circuits unusually active.

stories.title: This common vitamin was linked to 13% better cognitive scores
stories.summary: Older adults with mild cognitive impairment and sleep problems who took at least 5,000 IU of vitamin D daily scored more than 13% higher on a cognitive test than those taking none.

stories.title: This shark can live 400 years. Its eyes barely seem to age
stories.summary: Greenland sharks may live for 400 years without suffering the kind of retinal decline normally associated with aging. Researchers found healthy eye tissue and active proteins specially adapted for seeing blue light in the dim Arctic depths.

stories.title: Quitting alcohol may prime the brain for relapse
stories.summary: Mice that developed compulsive drinking after alcohol abstinence showed more than double the activity in a brain region associated with stress and addiction. Because the signal appeared before they drank again, researchers think it could eventually help predict who is most at risk of relapse.

stories.title: Exercise may work better for keeping weight off than losing it
stories.summary: Exercise may not be a powerful weight-loss tool on its own, but it appears to play a much bigger role in preventing lost weight from returning.

stories.title: This gut microbe may help keep you strong as you age
stories.summary: Scientists have linked a specific gut bacterium, Roseburia inulinivorans, to stronger muscles in both humans and mice. Older adults who carried it had 29% greater handgrip strength, while treated mice gained about 30% more grip strength and developed larger, more fast-twitch muscle fibers.

stories.title: This weight-loss hormone may protect the liver even without weight loss
stories.summary: A hormone already known for curbing appetite and supporting weight loss may have a surprising second job: protecting the liver from inflammation and scarring.

stories.title: Ozempic does something unexpected to the brain’s hunger neurons
stories.summary: Ozempic may work in the brain in almost the opposite way scientists expected, activating hunger-linked neurons that appear essential for sustaining fat loss. The surprising discovery in mice could reveal new targets for developing even more effective obesity drugs.

stories.title: Knee osteoarthritis isn’t inevitable — here’s what you can do
stories.summary: Knee osteoarthritis can seriously affect mobility and quality of life, but its progression isn’t completely out of your control. Exercise, stronger leg muscles, a healthier diet, and even modest weight loss can dramatically reduce stress on the knees and help keep pain in check.

stories.title: AI-designed “intrabodies” could unlock new treatments for Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and MND
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a new way to turn ordinary antibodies into tiny disease-fighting molecules that can work inside human cells, potentially opening new paths for treating Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, Huntington’s disease, and motor neurone disease.

stories.title: Scientists turn probiotic bacteria into tiny drug factories for pancreatic cancer
stories.summary: Engineered probiotic bacteria were able to infiltrate pancreatic tumors, stimulate cancer-fighting immune cells, and slow tumor growth in animal studies. Even more strikingly, the treatment worked better when combined with chemotherapy, radiation, or immunotherapy.

stories.title: Low-fat vegan diet helps people lose weight without eating less
stories.summary: A low-fat vegan diet may help people lose weight without counting calories, shrinking portions, or feeling constantly hungry.

stories.title: A little-known protein may be fueling Alzheimer’s — and scientists found a way to block it
stories.summary: An experimental Alzheimer’s compound prevented damaging protein clumps from forming in the brains of mice, helping nerve cells survive longer and reducing amyloid buildup.

stories.title: This 10-cent heart drug cuts hospitalizations by 25%
stories.summary: A centuries-old heart drug costing less than ten cents a day could help keep heart-failure patients out of the hospital. New research suggests low-dose digoxin can reduce heart-failure hospitalizations by about 25%, potentially paving the way for its return as a major treatment.

stories.title: A little movement in midlife could pay off for your brain years later
stories.summary: Exercise and healthy blood sugar levels in midlife may help slow cognitive decline decades later. Physical activity appeared especially beneficial for Mexican American adults, suggesting that some brain-protective factors may differ across populations.

stories.title: The common mistake that could make aging joints hurt more
stories.summary: Aging gradually wears down the cartilage and fluid that protect our joints, but avoiding movement may actually make matters worse. Exercise helps nourish cartilage, strengthens the muscles that protect joints, and can reduce osteoarthritis pain.

stories.title: Scientists solve the mystery of a brain “switch” that can trigger weight loss in opposite ways
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered why two seemingly opposite ways of targeting the same brain receptor can both promote weight loss. In mice, activating the GIP receptor in the brainstem reduced appetite, while blocking it in the hypothalamus removed a kind of “brake” on fullness signals.

stories.title: Immune cells flood into the aging brain, Stanford scientists discover
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that the aging human brain may be far less isolated from the rest of the body than once believed.

stories.title: A stress hormone may help the brain repair itself
stories.summary: A surprising stress-related signal may help the brain repair itself after injury. Researchers found that myelin-producing precursor cells rapidly release the stress hormone CRH near damaged brain tissue, helping control how those cells mature and rebuild protective nerve insulation.

stories.title: Women taking estrogen had fewer signs of Alzheimer’s in their brains
stories.summary: Women who used estrogen-only hormone therapy later in life were less likely to develop dementia and showed fewer signs of Alzheimer’s disease in their brains, according to a large study of more than 21,000 participants.

stories.title: This common vitamin deficiency becomes far more dangerous when paired with belly fat
stories.summary: A large study of more than 5,500 adults over 50 found a striking combination of risk factors: abdominal obesity paired with vitamin D deficiency was linked to a 123% higher risk of death over six years.

stories.title: Drinking orange juice every day may change thousands of genes
stories.summary: Orange juice may have a much bigger effect on the body than scientists once realized. Drinking it regularly appears to influence genes tied to inflammation, blood pressure, metabolism, and blood sugar control, while studies have also found improvements in cholesterol and blood vessel health.

stories.title: A surprising brain discovery could help explain why we overeat fatty foods
stories.summary: A protein inside appetite-controlling brain cells may play an important role in preventing overeating and obesity, particularly when high-fat foods are readily available.

stories.title: Human brain cells are far more powerful than scientists thought
stories.summary: A single human brain cell may be far more powerful than scientists once realized. Researchers found that cortical neurons can perform remarkably complex computations, giving them capabilities more like tiny biological computers than simple on-off switches.

stories.title: Scientists discover the brain has a fast lane and slow lane for clearing waste
stories.summary: AI has helped scientists measure the brain’s hidden cleaning system, revealing that fluid moves rapidly around its outer spaces but about 50 times more slowly through deep tissue.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden brain rhythm that could improve Parkinson’s treatment
stories.summary: Scientists have pinpointed a brain network—and its distinctive electrical rhythm—that appears to drive the benefits of deep brain stimulation for Parkinson’s disease. The discovery could lead to more precise, personalized stimulation settings and better results for patients.

stories.title: Scientists turn sheep’s wool into a material that helps regrow bone
stories.summary: Keratin extracted from sheep’s wool helped damaged bone regenerate in animals, producing tissue that was more organized and structurally similar to healthy bone than tissue grown with conventional collagen scaffolds.

stories.title: MIT neuroscientists discover the brain can reason without words
stories.summary: MIT neuroscientists have found striking evidence that language and logical reasoning are powered by separate systems in the brain.

stories.title: A daily glass of fruit juice was linked to lower depression scores
stories.summary: A daily glass of 100% fruit juice or a smoothie may help improve more than just fruit intake. In a small four-week trial, participants who added one to a healthier diet showed significantly lower depression scores, hinting that a simple dietary change could also support mental well-being.

stories.title: For decades, we were told to choose low-fat dairy. New research says otherwise
stories.summary: Full-fat dairy may be healthier than conventional advice has suggested. In a 12-week study, adults who ate three servings a day showed no meaningful increases in weight, body fat, cholesterol, or insulin resistance.

stories.title: Scientists say just 7 days of meditation can rewire your brain
stories.summary: An intensive seven-day meditation retreat triggered striking changes across the brain and body, including shifts tied to neuroplasticity, immunity, metabolism, and natural pain relief.

stories.title: Cutting sweet foods doesn’t curb cravings or improve health
stories.summary: Changing how much sweet-tasting food people eat may not change how much they crave or enjoy sweetness after all. In a six-month trial, researchers found that people assigned to high-, low-, or average-sweetness diets showed no meaningful differences in their preference for sweet foods, body weight,…

stories.title: Vitamin C may fight cancer — but not the way scientists once thought
stories.summary: Linus Pauling was widely mocked for claiming that vitamin C could fight cancer, especially after trials using vitamin C pills showed no benefit.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden brain shift that begins around age 50
stories.summary: Beginning around age 50, the brain’s memory center appears to lose many of its longtime immune cells and replace them with more inflammatory ones. This surprising shift may help explain how normal aging sets the stage for Alzheimer’s disease and dementia.

stories.title: Nearly half of dementia cases may be linked to risks you can change
stories.summary: A long-term brain study found that common risks such as smoking, high blood pressure, heart disease, and high blood lipids were strongly linked to damage associated with vascular dementia.

stories.title: A drug already used for osteoporosis blocked spinal damage in a new study
stories.summary: Genetic changes may set off a chain reaction that causes the spine’s natural shock absorbers to harden and deteriorate. Zebrafish with a faulty collagen-related gene developed mineral buildup and spinal fusion similar to human disc disease.

stories.title: Scientists discover the brain cells that keep you motivated
stories.summary: A group of brain cells called orexin neurons appears to help us keep working when reaching a reward becomes increasingly difficult.

stories.title: A common sugar may help cancer cells break free and spread
stories.summary: Chemotherapy-surviving ovarian cancer cells may release fructose to help neighboring tumor cells loosen, escape, and spread. The discovery suggests that sugary diets and cholesterol-lowering drugs could influence cancer progression, though the effects have not yet been confirmed in patients.

stories.title: Two new compounds could reveal hidden drivers of Alzheimer’s disease
stories.summary: Vanderbilt researchers created the first selective compound designed to inhibit TAOK-1, a poorly understood protein connected to Alzheimer’s disease. They also discovered a second compound that activates the entire TAOK protein family, offering scientists an unexpected new research tool.

stories.title: Without this protein, damaged muscle turns to fat and scar tissue
stories.summary: A protein once thought to mainly protect chromosome ends may also be essential for keeping muscle stem cells ready to repair injuries. Researchers found that TRF2 helps these cells maintain their identity and coordinate the cycle of rest, repair, and renewal.

stories.title: Eating less protein could slow aging, major review finds
stories.summary: A sweeping review of more than 350 studies suggests that the protein boom may be overselling what many people actually need. Eating less protein appears to improve metabolism, reduce inflammation and cellular damage, and activate pathways linked to healthier aging and longer life.

stories.title: Eating one avocado a day may lower heart disease risk
stories.summary: A daily avocado may help lower heart disease risk in adults with obesity by reducing the number of LDL particles circulating in the blood. After six months, participants who ate an avocado each day experienced a decline associated with an estimated 4% reduction in cardiovascular risk.

stories.title: Scientists may have found a way to prevent statin muscle pain
stories.summary: Scientists have identified an immune response that may explain why statins cause muscle pain, weakness, and exercise intolerance in some people. The finding could eventually lead to treatments that protect muscles while preserving the drugs’ lifesaving cardiovascular benefits.

stories.title: Scientists discover why poor sleep may harm some brains more
stories.summary: A gene involved in the brain’s overnight cleaning system may change how strongly poor sleep affects Alzheimer’s-related brain changes. The findings point toward more personalized prevention strategies based on both genetics and sleep habits.

stories.title: AI can tell if your brain is aging faster than you are
stories.summary: A person’s sleeping brain may reveal warning signs of dementia long before memory problems begin. Researchers used machine learning to analyze EEG recordings from about 7,000 adults and found that an older-than-expected “brain age” was tied to a sharply higher dementia risk.

stories.title: Scientists discover how obesity may fuel Alzheimer’s disease
stories.summary: Researchers have uncovered a possible biological pathway connecting obesity to Alzheimer’s disease. Obesity appears to raise levels of certain fat molecules that can travel to the brain, disrupt its immune defenses, and promote harmful amyloid buildup.

stories.title: Scientists find a simple routine linked to less pain and depression
stories.summary: Keeping a regular daily schedule may help reduce pain and depression, especially among older adults with insomnia. Researchers found that consistent times for waking, eating, socializing, and sleeping were linked to better well-being regardless of sleep quality.

stories.title: Rice bran compound may help ease irritable bowel symptoms
stories.summary: A compound in rice bran may help calm an overactive gut by reducing the calcium signals that cause intestinal muscles to contract. Ferulic acid suppressed contractions triggered by several chemical messengers in laboratory experiments.

stories.title: Daily multivitamin may help older adults stay independent
stories.summary: Taking a daily multivitamin may help older adults preserve the strength and stamina needed for everyday activities. After three years, users reported better functional health than those taking a placebo, although the preliminary findings still require peer review.

stories.title: Your gut may help your brain decide what to remember
stories.summary: Signals traveling from the gut to the brain may help turn meals into lasting memories. Rats showed stronger memory activity after consuming nutritious foods, but not after drinking sweet liquids with little or no nutritional value.

stories.title: Eating within 8 hours may help keep the aging brain sharp
stories.summary: Eating within a shorter daily window may help protect certain thinking skills as people age. In a small six-month trial, older women who limited eating to about 8 to 9 hours a day performed better on planning and problem-solving tests than those who ate over 12 hours.

stories.title: A hidden Alzheimer’s tipping point may decide who gets dementia
stories.summary: Scientists have identified a possible tipping point that helps determine whether Alzheimer’s-related brain changes lead to dementia. The key may lie in how the brain’s immune cells respond to plaques and tau, offering a promising new target for treatments designed to extend cognitive resilience.

stories.title: Superagers keep youthful memories but their DNA does not explain why
stories.summary: Scientists expected SuperAgers might simply inherit fewer Alzheimer’s-related risks, but their genes looked much like those of typical older adults. Their extraordinary memories may instead come from still-unknown protective forces involving the brain, body, lifestyle, and environment.

stories.title: AI helps Stanford scientists discover “natural Ozempic” without the usual side effects
stories.summary: Stanford Medicine researchers have discovered a naturally occurring molecule that may suppress appetite and reduce body weight much like Ozempic, but without several of its common side effects.

stories.title: APOE2 may protect the brain from Alzheimer’s and aging
stories.summary: The longevity-linked APOE2 gene appears to protect brain cells by reducing DNA damage and helping neurons recover from stress. The finding could open a new path toward treatments that mimic APOE2’s defenses in people at higher genetic risk for Alzheimer’s.

stories.title: Ozempic and Mounjaro linked to a surprising hair loss risk
stories.summary: A large study suggests that GLP-1 drugs including Ozempic and Mounjaro may slightly increase the risk of hair loss in people with type 2 diabetes.

stories.title: Cerebral small vessel disease: new treatment possibilities for the little-known condition affecting millions of people
stories.summary: This little-known brain disorder is currently one of the biggest challenges facing medicine where age-related diseases are concerned.

stories.title: Lab-grown mini brains may predict which Alzheimer’s treatments will work
stories.summary: Miniature brain models grown from patients’ cells revealed striking differences in how Alzheimer’s-related tissue responds to an antidepressant. The organoids and the particles they release could eventually guide more personalized treatments and provide new clues for diagnosing the disease.

stories.title: Coffee may protect your heart but energy drinks could harm it
stories.summary: For most adults, a daily caffeine habit may be safer for the heart than many people assume. A new American Heart Association review found that up to 400 milligrams of caffeine a day, roughly three to five cups of regular black coffee, is generally safe and may even be linked to lower risks of heart…

stories.title: Scientists detect hidden skin damage before it becomes visible
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a hidden warning sign of skin damage that appears before collagen fibers visibly thin, break, or lose their connections.

stories.title: Alzheimer’s breakthrough: Scientists restore two hours of sleep without clearing brain plaques
stories.summary: Researchers have uncovered a surprising culprit behind sleep loss in Alzheimer’s disease: the brain’s own immune cells. In mice with amyloid plaques, overactive microglia triggered inflammation that kept the brain from getting enough deep, restorative sleep.

stories.title: UCLA scientists develop mineral sunscreen without the chalky white cast
stories.summary: Scientists have redesigned zinc oxide particles to create a mineral sunscreen that protects against ultraviolet radiation without leaving such a noticeable white cast. The SPF 30 formula could make sunscreen easier and more appealing to use across a wider range of skin tones.

stories.title: Mediterranean diet may activate tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain
stories.summary: The Mediterranean diet may influence aging through tiny proteins produced inside the cell’s mitochondria. Older adults who followed the diet most closely had higher levels of humanin and SHMOOSE, which have been linked to heart and brain protection.

stories.title: Popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
stories.summary: Several popular sugar substitutes may not be as harmless as they seem. Adults who consumed the most artificial sweeteners showed substantially faster declines in memory and thinking, especially if they were under 60 or had diabetes.

stories.title: New Alzheimer's drug repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
stories.summary: A drug originally developed for spinal cord injury may offer a fresh approach to treating Alzheimer’s disease. In mouse studies, KCL-286 repaired dangerous DNA damage, reduced inflammation, and targeted multiple disease-related pathways instead of focusing on just amyloid or tau.

stories.title: EastDiet lowers risk of heart disease by 22% and belly fat by 17%
stories.summary: China's eastern coastal region is associated with lower obesity, cardiovascular risk, and higher life expectancy. It's also where, for generations, market stalls selling fresh leafy greens, lotus seed pods, vegetables, tofu, and freshwater fish have shaped the diet of those living there.

stories.title: Going to museums, movies, and theater may help your body stay younger
stories.summary: Going to the cinema, visiting museums, or attending concerts may do more than entertain. Researchers found that older adults who regularly participated in cultural activities tended to have bodies that functioned like those of people about three years younger.

stories.title: Chewing bubble gum after beetroot may help lower blood pressure
stories.summary: A new study found that chewing sugary gum after eating nitrate-rich vegetables or drinking beetroot juice helped the body produce more beneficial nitrite, leading to a temporary drop in blood pressure.

stories.title: Popular weight-loss drugs Ozempic and Wegovy may slow biological aging
stories.summary: Researchers found that semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, slowed biological aging markers in adults with HIV, marking the first clinical evidence that the drug may influence human aging.

stories.title: Exercise doesn't just strengthen the heart. It rewires it
stories.summary: Exercise doesn't just make the heart stronger. It also rewires the nerves that regulate it, a discovery that could pave the way for more personalized treatments for common heart conditions such as arrhythmias and angina.

stories.title: Losing just 80 minutes of sleep a night could make you gain weight
stories.summary: Sleeping about an hour and 20 minutes less each night for six weeks caused participants to gain weight and spend more time inactive. Researchers found that even mild, realistic sleep loss, similar to what many adults experience, had measurable effects.

stories.title: Scientists discovered the brain doesn't make decisions the way we thought
stories.summary: A new study suggests the brain begins making decisions much earlier than scientists previously thought. Researchers found that even primary sensory regions are influenced by higher brain areas through rapid feedback loops, rather than simply passing information forward.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden heart valve risk linked to gum disease
stories.summary: Researchers found that bacteria linked to gum disease may help drive the development of calcific aortic valve stenosis by triggering inflammation and calcium buildup in the heart valve.
